supersedes.why: v2 covered 30 of the 44 executions and knew only two capture carriers. Since it was written, 8 more landed by transcription, 6 landed by a THIRD carrier that did not exist then - the agent's own durable final-message file - and 4 of those are re-executions after the watchdog loss recorded as E-29. An index that stopped at v2 would omit fourteen executions and misdescribe six, which is the silence OW-18 scores as a false claim.

extracted_from_transcript.why: runtime-held carrier: the agent could not alter it after the fact

extracted_from_authored_file.why: the agent wrote the carrier itself: durable and re-readable, but not tamper-evident against its author, so Layer A is NOT restored

transcribed_from_notification.why: no durable carrier existed; the orchestrator copied the agent's words out of a notification in its own context

two_claims_not_one.re_derivable_today: whether a durable artifact still backs the record. ALWAYS MEASURED.
two_claims_not_one.capture_at_land_time: how the record was actually produced. MEASURED where a transcript survives, DISCLOSED where the record testifies against itself, REPORTED where only the orchestrator's account of its own procedure covers it.

known_imprecision_stated_rather_than_hid: The durable copies of the first 30 records are all named layer_a_*, including the 2 that were TRANSCRIBED and are therefore Layer C. A filename is a claim, so every record below carries both the layer its FILENAME implies and the layer that is actually true, and the mismatches are counted. The files are NOT being renamed: v1 and v2 reference them by those names, and rewriting history to tidy a label is the worse error. New records are named for their true layer.
honest_limits: For 28 executions, capture_at_land_time rests on the orchestrator's account of its own procedure. That is the weakest tier in this file and it is named as such rather than presented as a finding.

re_derivable_today is a statement about today. It will degrade further as transcripts age, and a future re-run of this index will show fewer, not more. That is a property of the harness, not of the records.
A tier says nothing about the scholarly quality of the review it carries. Chain of custody and scholarship are separate axes.

The two TRANSCRIBED records each carry a MEASURED deliverable digest equal to the transcribed one, and the landing tool verified record-to-deliverable parity over rows_reviewed and the recomputed tally. That corroboration is real and does NOT upgrade the tier.

For the 28 pre-OW-18 executions, capture_at_land_time still rests on the orchestrator's account of its own procedure - REPORTED, the weakest tier in this file. v3 does not upgrade it, because nothing new was measured about those executions; only their durable copies were re-digested.

still_backed_by_a_durable_artifact_today is a statement about TODAY. Session scratchpads are not permanent, so the 6 authored-file records and the 10 transcribed source files will stop being re-derivable when this session's scratch is cleared. The landed packets and receipts under SP are the durable scholarly record and are unaffected.

A re-execution's record describes only that execution. The killed #e1 executions produced nothing, and their absence is recorded as UNAVAILABLE in E-29 rather than represented here as a gap in coverage.

layer_filename_claim_audit.basis: a mismatch is counted only where BOTH the filename's implied layer and the true layer are known. An unknown is counted separately and never as a mismatch - counting unknowns as wrong is how a provenance report starts crying wolf.
